images.filename: Mike Harmon Wrecked Bristol Car International Motorsports Hall of Fame.jpg
images.caption: Back when me and my Dad went on a trip to Atlanta and then went down to Talladega for the spring weekend in 2011, we visited the Motorsports Hall of Fame museum by the track and came across this rather famous piece of wrecked machinery, the car in which Mike Harmon destroyed during practice at the Bristol Motor Speedway for the 2002 Food City 250 in the then known NASCAR Busch series. His car shot up the track and he crashed into an entry gate coming off turn 2 which sheared his car apart completely and left him exposed to oncoming traffic, but thankfully Johnny Sauter drove low enough to avoid striking him, and Harmon amazingly walked away unharmed. The crash was eerily similar to when Michael Waltrip struck the same area during a Busch series race in 1990 which also tore his car apart, in which Waltrip also escaped serious injury too.

The crash was eerily similar to when Michael Waltrip struck the same area during a Busch series race in 1990 which also tore his car apart, in which Waltrip also escaped serious injury too.

images.filename: Buck Baker 1957 Chevy Bel Air International Motorsports Hall of Fame.jpg
images.caption: The first driver to win consecutive titles in NASCAR in 1956 and 1957, Buck Baker's 1957 #87 Chevrolet Bel Air car on display at the International Motorsports Hall of Fame Museum.
images.alt: The first driver to win consecutive titles in NASCAR in 1956 and 1957, Buck Baker's 1957 #87 Chevrolet Bel Air car on display at the International Motorsports Hall of Fame Museum.

images.filename: Richard Petty Dodge Charger International Motorsports Hall of Fame.jpg
images.caption: One of the many iconic STP cars that Richard Petty drove in his illustrious NASCAR career, this Dodge Charger from 1976 when he finished 2nd in the Winston Cup Championship to Cale Yarborough, on display at the International Motorsports Hall of Fame museum.
images.alt: One of the many iconic STP cars that Richard Petty drove in his illustrious NASCAR career, this Dodge Charger from 1976 when he finished 2nd in the Winston Cup Championship to Cale Yarborough, on display at the International Motorsports Hall of Fame museum.

images.filename: Dale Earnhardt 1997 Chevy Monte Carlo International Motorsports Hall of Fame.jpg
images.caption: One of the cars Dale Earnhardt drove in the 1997 NASCAR Winston Cup season on display at the International Motorsports Hall of Fame museum. Dale made himself famous driving the iconic black GM Goodwrench car, in which he garnered his famous nickname "The Intimidator" for his style of driving which involved moving other drivers out of the way and making him either loved or hated among the fans. 1997 was the first year of his career where he went winless since 1981.

images.filename: Tiny Lund 1964 Ford Galaxie International Motorsports Hall of Fame.jpg
images.caption: One of the most iconic cars that drove in NASCAR in the 1960s, this Ford Galaxie that was piloted by the 1963 Daytona 500 winner Tiny Lund on display at the International Motorsports Hall of Fame museum.
images.alt: One of the most iconic cars that drove in NASCAR in the 1960s, this Ford Galaxie that was piloted by the 1963 Daytona 500 winner Tiny Lund on display at the International Motorsports Hall of Fame museum.

images.filename: Buddy Baker 1969 Dodge Daytona International Motorsports Hall of Fame.jpg
images.caption: One of the most ground breaking cars in NASCAR history, the 1969 Dodge Charger Daytona on display at the International Motorsports Hall of Fame museum. This was the car that Buddy Baker drove to the first ever 200 mph run during a closed test session at the Talladega Superspeedway in March 1970, clocking in an accurate speed of 200.447 mph.
